risks.risk_description: Risk arising from economic shockwaves, geopolitical tensions, and market changes impacting financial stability, supply chains, customer behavior, and business continuity.

risk_driver.driver_description: Cost-of-living and cost-of-doing-business crises, tighter monetary policy, higher interest rates, and inflation.
War in Ukraine, tensions between US and China, and weakening of globalisation bonds.
Changing customer behavior, competition, and supply chain disruptions.
Increasing due diligence and compliance requirements related to sustainable development and third-party risks.

risk_recommendations: Evaluate effectiveness of mechanisms to identify, assess, and monitor macroeconomic and geopolitical changes.
Assess adequacy of strategic investment in R&D to remain competitive globally.
Ensure financial stress testing and scenario planning are aligned with emerging risks.
Adopt agile and adaptive strategies to manage fast-moving risks.
Advise on processes to adapt and mitigate macroeconomic and geopolitical risks.
Evaluate internal controls for compliance with regulations such as sanctions and anti-money laundering.
Coordinate efforts across three lines of defense to capture interrelated risks.
Recruit and train staff with knowledge and skills to understand emerging risks.
Use data analytics and predictive advisory services to support risk management.
Follow up on implementation of critical strategic decisions.
risks.trend: Ranked joint 3rd highest risk in 2024, highest since 2018. Expected to be 5th largest risk in 2027. Market changes would rank 2nd in economic downturn.
risks.impact: Risks include insolvency, financial instability, disrupted supply chains, and failure to attract/retain skills, threatening long-term business sustainability.
risk_event: Germany slipping into recession following energy price shock in 2023.
Economic effects of higher inflation and interest rates impacting businesses.
Silicon Valley Bank failure illustrating risks of outdated assumptions.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to cyberattacks, data breaches, and evolving digital threats impacting organisational networks and data integrity.

risk_driver.driver_description: Professionalisation and commercialisation of hacking, state-sponsored wiper attacks, and weaponisation of cyberattacks.
Cloud migration, digitalisation of operational technologies, and integration with suppliers increasing vulnerabilities.
Use of AI and blockchain adding complexity and new risk exposures.
Increasing regulations such as GDPR, EU Cyber Resilience Act, NIS2, DORA, and mandatory compliance requirements.
Difficulty attracting and retaining skilled cybersecurity professionals.

risk_recommendations: Assess compliance with cybersecurity laws, regulations, and industry standards.
Align risk taxonomies and controls across three lines of defense.
Enhance collaboration between CISO, internal audit, and board.
Evaluate effectiveness of cybersecurity controls and vulnerability assessments.
Monitor cybersecurity posture continuously and assess incident response plans.
Implement cybersecurity awareness and training programs.
Ensure backup data integrity and rapid recovery capabilities.
Communicate cybersecurity risks clearly to senior management and board.
Use certifications like ISO 27001 to develop detailed business continuity plans.
Focus on technical risk-based assessments beyond compliance audits.
risks.trend: Maintains top risk position with 84% citing it as top five risk in 2024, slightly up from 82% in previous years. Expected to remain number one threat in 2027.
risks.impact: Potential for severe operational disruption, data loss, reputational damage, and regulatory penalties. Increasing complexity and evolving threat landscape.
risk_event: Ransomware attacks on British Airways, Boots, and BBC via payroll provider software in UK.
Increased cyberattacks following Sweden's NATO membership announcement.
Use of AI-generated malware targeting specific vulnerabilities.

risks.risk_name: Human Capital, Diversity, Talent Management and Retention
risks.risk_description: Risks arising from challenges in attracting, retaining, and managing talent, including cultural misalignment and psychological well-being issues.

risk_driver.driver_description: Structural talent shortages accelerated by the pandemic and economic conditions.
Demand for flexible working, social purpose alignment, and diversity.
Corporate culture lagging behind social changes and employee expectations.
Increased stress and isolation due to hybrid working and economic uncertainty.
Difficulty recruiting and retaining skilled internal audit professionals with diverse backgrounds.

risk_recommendations: Assess competitiveness of diversity, equality, inclusion, and work-life balance policies.
Ensure alignment and clear communication of organisational values and objectives.
Evaluate career progression, training, and promotion policies for talent attraction and retention.
Ensure compliance and effectiveness of diversity and inclusion controls.
Assess psychological safety and employee willingness to speak up.
Evaluate employee engagement surveys, exit interviews, and feedback mechanisms.
Adopt hybrid internal audit methodologies balancing formal audits and rapid assessments.
Promote internal audit as a management training ground with visible talent pipelines.
Develop talent management programs linked with HR departments including growth plans and rotations.
Foster empathetic leadership and communication beyond risk registers.
risks.trend: Ranked 2nd biggest risk in 2024 with 58% citing it as top five risk, up from 50% in 2023 and 40% in 2022. Expected to remain 2nd most challenging issue in 2027.
risks.impact: Failure to manage human capital risks can lead to strategic goal failure, increased attrition, reduced organisational resilience, and negative impacts on culture and morale.

risks.risk_name: Climate Change, Biodiversity and Environmental Sustainability
risks.risk_description: Risks related to environmental impacts, regulatory compliance, data quality, and reputational damage arising from climate change and sustainability challenges.

risk_driver.driver_description: Wildfires, floods, and other climate phenomena impacting supply chains and infrastructure.
New and evolving regulations such as CSRD, ESRS, TCFD, and EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive.
Poor quality and lack of standardised sustainability data hindering compliance and reporting.
Greenwashing accusations and shifting consumer preferences driving reputational and financial risks.
Need to assess both environmental impact and social/biodiversity effects of business activities.

risk_recommendations: Assess alignment of sustainability goals with business strategy and clear metrics.
Evaluate robustness of climate and environmental objectives based on data and regulations.
Assess adequacy of implementation plans to meet sustainability objectives.
Evaluate risk management and controls related to sustainability.
Ensure compliance with current and forthcoming environmental regulations and reporting requirements.
Monitor environmental performance and continuous improvement mechanisms.
Engage stakeholders including specialist NGOs for expertise and knowledge.
Assess integration of sustainability goals in supplier contracts.
Conduct enterprise-wide climate readiness audits and share best practices.
Focus on entrepreneurial strategies beyond mere compliance.
risks.trend: Ranked 7th in 2024 with 31% citing it as top five risk, down from 6th place and 38% in 2023. Expected to rise to 3rd place by 2027 due to new regulations and stakeholder interest.
risks.impact: Potential impacts include supply chain disruptions, regulatory penalties, reputational damage, and failure to meet sustainability commitments.
risk_event: Wildfires in Greece in 2023 destroying livelihoods and holidays.
European Parliament relabelling gas and nuclear energy as sustainable in 2022, causing investor and campaigner backlash.

risks.risk_name: Supply Chain, Outsourcing and 'Nth' Party Risk
risks.risk_description: Risks arising from dependencies on suppliers and third parties, including geopolitical tensions, insolvencies, regulatory compliance, and physical disruptions.

risk_driver.driver_description: War in Ukraine, US-China tensions, and weakening global trade impacting supply chains.
Rising costs, inflation, and supplier insolvencies increasing supply chain vulnerabilities.
New due diligence and sustainability reporting requirements such as EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive and CSRD.
Extreme weather events and incidents like the Ever Given grounding highlighting fragility of physical supply chains.
Legislation encouraging reshoring and reducing dependence on certain regions.

risk_recommendations: Assess resilience of supply chains to macroeconomic and geopolitical risks.
Monitor supplier challenges and implement early detection mechanisms.
Conduct due diligence on potential suppliers for strategic alignment.
Review outsourcing contracts for regulatory compliance.
Update vendor management frameworks for selection and performance monitoring.
Evaluate third-party and vendor compliance and performance.
Ensure effective business continuity and crisis management plans with scenario testing.
Define and implement governance structures across three lines for supply chain risk management.
Support diversification of supply sources and investment in alternative materials.
Engage in scenario planning for low-likelihood, high-impact supply chain disruptions.
risks.trend: Ranked 8th in 2024 with 30% citing it as top five risk, maintaining position from previous year. Expected to drop to 9th place by 2027, while business continuity efforts rise to 2nd place.
risks.impact: Risks include operational disruption, increased costs, compliance failures, reputational damage, and loss of competitive advantage.
risk_event: Ever Given container ship grounding in Suez Canal illustrating supply chain fragility.
Flooding in Germany in 2021 causing supply chain stress.
EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive adoption in 2023.
